Subject: Fwd: Q1 spike — internal reconciliation options

Team — forwarding Aurora's usage export. I ran a quick model (see attached) with three resolution options:

Option A — One-time invoice for exact overage: $18,960 (list price at $0.016/token for overage buckets).
Option B — Apply 30% commercial credit to overage and invoice remainder: $13,272 + goodwill of $5,688 credit.
Option C — Waive X% now and convert X tokens into added committed capacity at a 20% discounted rate for the 12-month renewal (reduces sticker and prevents future spikes).

My recommendation: Option B + include capacity uplift in the renewal (hybrid). That keeps the relationship healthy and preserves revenue while giving Aurora predictable unit economics. If we amortize the invoice over the 12-month renewal as a one-time prepayment, billing can tie it to the new capacity SKU.

Attachments: aurora-overage-draft.xlsx (internal calc)

Can finance give a greenlight on the credit band? Ben — can you confirm the max % we can approve pre-Sales Ops escalation? Vivek — any compliance/contract flags if we roll the overage into an amendment?

Thanks,
Priya
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Q1 spike — internal reconciliation options

+1 on Option B. Recommend 25–35% credit band given their ARR and fast ramp. If we apply a 30% credit, we can approve without exec escalation. Amortizing across the renewal to smooth cash/concerns is fine — cash still follows invoice.

No Compliance flags from my side for rolling into an amendment; keep language explicit about one-off and non-recurring nature of the waived portion.

Ben
VP, Revenue Operations
